lockup.summary: The company, its directors and officers, and nearly all other holders agreed not to sell shares for at least 180 days after the prospectus date, unless ThinkEquity LLC agrees in writing.

what: Akston is a pet biotech company that develops biologic medicines for cats, dogs and other companion animals.
proceeds: It expects net proceeds of about $16.1 million. It plans to finish a new manufacturing facility, make batches of its lead dog cancer drug, run studies in dogs and cats, and cover general costs.
risks: Akston is young, has lost a lot of money since it began, expects more losses, and so its future is hard to judge.
Its controls for catching errors and fraud in its reporting may fail to find every problem.
Its business depends on customers, who may face rising costs and lower income.
Customers merging into larger groups could push down the prices Akston can charge for its products.
Limits may restrict how much Akston can use its past tax losses to reduce future taxable income.
